pre_process: additional_context = "Use the pack_stocks helper from solver_lib to implement a first-fit bin-packing routine that (1) respects each piece's min/max counts, (2) tries both orientations per stock_type, (3) greedily fills existing stocks of the same type before opening new ones, and (4) only opens the minimal number of stocks needed. This will reduce waste and reach the archive best-known objective of 0.140 on assortment_problem."
rationale:
## Diagnosis
assortment_problem is failing with systematic "Piece count violation" errors (min count not met, e.g. required min=20 but allocated=0) because the generated solver only attempts a single orientation per piece type and never guarantees minimum quantities across all piece types; this stems from the depth-2/3 pre_process guidance promising a pack_stocks helper that was never reliably emitted or was malformed, leaving the solver to emit naive per-piece allocation that under-allocates when max constraints or orientation choices make single-stock packing impossible. This affects only assortment_problem (largest gap 0.140, mean=0.000) while other tasks remain frozen.

## Intervention
Add solver_lib:pack_stocks providing a reusable first-fit-with-orientation allocator that (a) groups pieces by type, (b) computes exact min/max counts per type, (c) tries both orientations per stock, (d) greedily fills existing same-type stocks before opening new ones, and (e) only opens the minimal number of stocks; the solve function is replaced to call this helper directly instead of the broken combinations loop. This targets only assortment_problem (addresses the exact count-violation failure mode that previous layers could not fix without breaking runtime).

## Why this is different
Depth-2/3 pre_process only injected textual guidance assuming an existing pack_stocks helper would be magically available; this layer emits the actual executable helper (previously promised but absent) plus a corrected solve that conditions on task metadata (min/max counts, stock_type) rather than re-emitting broken combinations code, producing a structurally different algorithm class (true min-count-aware first-fit vs. naive per-piece) that can reach the archive best-known 0.140 without regressions to frozen tasks.
